name: The Binding

meta.previous: Tome of the Cabal (Alliance, 3)orTome of the Cabal (Horde, 3)

summary: Above Ratchet, warlocks face the rite that binds a felhunter to their will. Strahad Farsan oversees the summoning with the restored Tome of the Cabal, drawing an aggressive demon from the Nether to be subdued in combat.

sections.title: The Cabal's Circle
sections.body: On Kalimdor's bluffs above Ratchet, the goblin port, Strahad Farsan conducts dangerous trials in demon summoning. After a warlock gathers the fragments and reagents needed to restore the ancient Tome of the Cabal, Strahad prepares the binding grounds. He lays an inner glyph of containment while his acolytes channel power through enchanted rods to complete the outer circle. The circles keep whatever emerges isolated from the settlement below.

sections.title: Subjugating the Hunter
sections.body: The Tome of the Cabal holds the incantations that open a bridge into the Twisting Nether. Felhunters are ravenous demonic hounds that hunger for arcane power and feast on magical energy. No gentle enthrallment or persuasion will bind one. The warlock must violently subdue and break the summoned beast in combat before it recognizes its rightful master. Surviving the clash proves the summoner can wield the hound against enemy spellcasters.

faq.q: What is the purpose of this ritual?
faq.answer: The ritual lets a warlock summon a felhunter and bind it to their will. Reading from the completed Tome of the Cabal inside Strahad Farsan's summoning circle draws the demon from the Nether. The warlock must defeat it in battle, winning its permanent service.

Strahad Farsan is an accomplished human warlock who works from a tower above Ratchet in the Barrens. His vast knowledge of dark summoning arts leads mentors from both the Alliance and the Horde to quietly send their most promising practitioners to study advanced binding rites under his tutelage.

faq.q: Why does a warlock have to kill the demon instead of enslaving it?
faq.answer: A felhunter is an aggressive predator that devours magic and respects absolute dominance. The practitioner must best it in physical and magical combat, breaking its ferocity and imprinting their authority over its spirit so it obeys future summonings.

faq.q: Can both Horde and Alliance warlocks perform this ritual here?
faq.answer: Yes. The steps to reconstruct the Tome of the Cabal differ by faction, but both Alliance and Horde warlocks are eventually directed to Strahad Farsan above Ratchet for the final summoning.

faq.q: What happens if the felhunter defeats the summoner?
faq.answer: If the summoner falls, the felhunter is banished to the Nether and the ritual fails. Warlocks who survive defeat can reclaim a fresh copy of the Tome of the Cabal from Strahad and try again when properly prepared.

faq.q: What makes felhunters unique compared to other demons?
faq.answer: Felhunters are demonic hounds that hunt by sensing magical emanations. They rely less on brute force or shadow spells, instead smelling out sorcery, devouring active enchantments, and disrupting enemy spellcasters. This makes them valuable companions against rival magic users.

angles.text: As a warlock, binding a felhunter marks a crucial milestone. The hound is a specialized anti-magic predator that can devour spells and shut down hostile casters.
As an Alliance warlock, you travel from Stormwind across the sea to neutral Ratchet, where Strahad oversees the perilous summoning ritual.
As a Horde warlock, you journey into the heart of the Barrens to prove your dominion over the Nether and bind the hound before Strahad on neutral ground.
